title: Subsurface Utility Engineering for a 22 kV Underground Cable Replacement Project: Methodology and Lessons Learned

record.title: Subsurface Utility Engineering for a 22 kV Underground Cable Replacement Project: Methodology and Lessons Learned
record.abstract: This book chapter describes the subsurface utility engineering process applied to a 3.4 km urban corridor in Zrenjanin, Serbia, where an ageing overhead 22 kV line was replaced by an underground cable. The chapter covers the full SUE quality level sequence from desk study through geophysical detection to test-hole verification. Desk-study sources included 1:2500 municipal cadastre sheets, utility operator records and historical aerial photographs from 1973 and 1988. GPR surveys with 250 MHz and 500 MHz antennas were conducted prior to open-cut construction; results were overlaid with cable route design drawings to identify conflict points. Seventeen previously unknown utility segments were discovered, triggering four route design revisions. The chapter discusses root causes of documentation gaps, including informal network extensions during the 1980s and post-war reconstruction, and proposes a project-phase checklist for Serbian distribution grid operators undertaking similar cable burial programmes.
